title: Shadow regression playbook and promptset heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, actionable playbook for (1) designing onboarding promptsets for chat-style assistants, (2) running shadow regressions when a new model or quantized variant is introduced, and (3) heuristics / lightweight metrics to triage regressions early. Meant to be a working checklist rather than a finished spec.

Context / motivation:
- We regularly bring new open models and quantized builds into the serving pipeline. Full eval suites are heavy; shadow/regression runs let us surface quality regressions and tool-calling breakages early against a production-like workload.
- Goal: detect regressions that materially affect product UX (tool calls, hallucination, persona drift, safety blocks) before rollout to production.

High-level concepts and definitions:
- Shadow run: execute the new model in parallel to the production model on sampled production prompts; do not return output to users. Record outputs and metrics.
- Promptset: curated set of chat prompts representing: happy-paths, edge cases, adversarial probes, multi-step tool interactions, persona-sensitive items, and safety probes. Keep ~600–1200 prompts in onboarding set (see sampling below).
- Tool-call fidelity: fraction of cases where the model triggers the same tool call (name + args shape) as the expected/reference.
- Safety choke points: short prompts that reliably trigger content-safety classifiers or equivocal outputs (useful for fast signal).

Promptset design guidelines (practical):
1) Coverage slices (explicit):
   - Persona anchors (10–20): short-system prompts that establish voice/tone; measured for style drift.
   - Tool synths (60–120): multi-turn dialogs that require the model to call a tool, pass structured args, and handle tool output. Include API error simulations.
   - Safety probes (80–150): deliberately ambiguous queries, policy-adjacent requests, and user intent obfuscation examples.
   - Factual recall / retrieval triggers (80–150): prompts requiring grounded facts; include retrieval stubs.
   - Compositional tasks (50–100): chain-of-thought like multi-step reasoning with explicit intermediate steps expected.
   - Short production samples (200): random sampled user turns from production (anonymized) to capture real distribution.

2) Prompt formatting rules:
   - Use canonical system prompt variants only (record variant id). Avoid ad-hoc system text.
   - Include explicit tool schema examples in the prompt where relevant.
   - For model-agnostic tests, normalize tokens where possible (e.g., replace long personal names with NAME_TOKEN).

3) Expectation artifacts per prompt:
   - expected_call: tool name or null
   - expected_args_shape: list of arg keys expected (use schema names)
   - expected_style_tags: [formal, concise, persona_x]
   - acceptable_alternatives: short list of acceptable paraphrases for nondeterministic outputs
   (Note: these are stored in the eval harness; not required in the onboarding doc here but plan to attach CSV rows during runs)

Shadow regression workflow (recipe):
1) Pre-run checks:
   - Confirm promptset version (tagged): onboarding/promptset/v2024-09-12
   - Confirm reference model (prod) id and new model id (include quantization/compilation flags)
   - Quick smoke: run 50 toy prompts locally to confirm API compatibility and tool ABI.
2) Shadow run (batching):
   - Execute promptset in randomized order with 3 independent seeds (deterministic sampling is fine for initial runs).
   - Record: raw outputs, tokenization lengths, logits (if available), predicted tool calls, and per-prompt timing breakdowns.
3) Basic signal extraction (automated):
   - Tool-call fidelity score (per prompt slice).
   - Hallucination proxy: fact-check mismatch rate on the retrieval/fact slice (using our lightweight exact-match checks and retrieval oracle).
   - Safety block rate: fraction where internal safety classifier flags refusal/overblock.
   - Persona divergence: cosine similarity over style embeddings (small SBERT) between reference and new model on persona slice.
   - Latency delta: p50/p95 token latency and end-to-end response latency.

Triage heuristics and thresholds (suggested, tuneable):
- Fail fast conditions (open regression ticket automatically):
  - tool-call fidelity drop > 5% absolute on the tool-synth slice AND >10 failing prompts total
  - hallucination proxy increase > 3% absolute on retrieval slice (stable across seeds)
  - safety-overblock increase > 1% absolute OR new unsafe outputs detected in safety probe set
  - p95 latency increase > 30% and p95 exceeds 800ms for chat completions

- Warning conditions (requires human review):
  - persona divergence score drop > 0.12 (cosine-based)
  - increases in tokenization length > 10% median (may indicate different tokenization heuristics from quantization)
  - tool calls with malformed args (schema mismatch) > 2%

Scripting checks (quick examples for the harness):
- Example query (pseudo):
  - expected = {"tool": "weather.get", "args": {"city": "San Francisco"}}
  - got = parse_tool(signal)
  - check: got.tool == expected.tool AND set(got.args.keys()) >= set(expected.args.keys())

- Regression rule (pseudocode):
  if (tool_fidelity_drop > 0.05 and failing_prompts > 10):
      create_jira('INF-REG', summary='Tool-call regression: ' + model_id)
      attach_artifacts([run_id, diff_samples.csv])

Interpreting false positives / common noise sources:
- Non-determinism: rerun seeds; persistent failures across seeds are meaningful.
- Prompt normalization mismatch: ensure canonical placeholders used in both reference and new model runs.
- Scheduled tokenization/compilation differences: quantized builds sometimes change tokenization splitting heuristics -> leads to length changes and formatting differences.
- Dataset leakage in sampled production prompts: anonymize and dedupe; repeated prompts can inflate metrics.

Regressions we care most about (priority order):
1) Tool-calling correctness (integrations break apps quickly).
2) Safety regressions (false negatives producing harmful content, or false positives blocking user flow).
3) Large semantic regressions (hallucination increases on retrieval tasks).
4) Latency regressions that violate SLO.

Quick examples (realistic-ish diffs to look for):
- Before: model returns tool call "price.lookup" with args {"symbol":"AAPL"}; After: model emits free-text reply referencing price but does not call tool -> tool_fidelity failure.
- Before: model refuses a policy-edge prompt with a short refusal; After: model returns content that skirted policy -> safety regression.
- Before: model returns structured JSON as requested; After: model adds extra commentary text before JSON causing downstream parser errors.

Operational notes / logging and artifacts to include in regression ticket:
- run_id, timestamp, model_ids, promptset version, random seed(s), raw_outputs.zip, parsed_tool_calls.csv, per-prompt timing.csv, top-20 diffs (human-friendly).
- Attach 10–20 representative transcriptions (good and bad) for reviewer context.

Human review rubric (for owners doing triage):
- Reproducibility: rerun failing prompt at least 3 times; record pass/fail.
- Severity: does it break an integration or produce unsafe output? (blocker if yes).
- Fixability: likely model issue vs. promptset mismatch vs. serving bug.
- Suggested mitigation: pin to previous model, add fallback routing, add targeted prompt engineering, or retrain/adjust quantization.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How often should we refresh the production-sampled portion? Monthly? Quarterly? (action: discuss with SRE + Product)
- Add a compact "tool-call delta visualization" in the console (heatmap by tool name vs. error type). (owner: Evan)
- Evaluate embedding-based persona metrics vs. simpler token-level heuristics for interpretability. (owner: Maya)
- Integrate with rollout automation so a failing shadow run halts canary promotion automatically. (Jira: INF-4201)

Quick checklist before model rollout:
- [ ] shadow run completed on full onboarding promptset (3 seeds)
- [ ] automated thresholds evaluated and results exported
- [ ] human triage completed for any warnings/failures
- [ ] regression ticket created if fail-fast condition met
- [ ] mitigations (pin/fallback) defined before canary

Notes / style and shorthand we use in the promptset CSVs:
- SYS_ID: identifier for system prompt variant
- PROMPT_ID: unique short key
- SLICE: persona/tool/safety/retrieval/compositional
- EXPECTED_TOOL: name or NULL

References / related pages:
- Prompt Onboarding Hub (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Prompt+Onboarding+Hub
- Prompt harness repo PR with tooling changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-harness/pull/78
- Example regression ticket template: INF-REG-TEMPLATE (Confluence)

If this doc looks useful, next iteration should: add a small JSON sample bundle (30 prompts) to run as a nightly sanity check, and wire the automatic ticket creation pipeline.

--Priya (notes)
